name: RelayOracle

methods.name: deploy
methods.desc:
Create. Caller becomes admin; guardian is a separate cold key.
`opup_app_id` is set once and has NO setter. It is a liveness dependency of every price post, so a mutable pointer would let a compromised admin aim it at an app that fails or does not exist and brick posting. The OpUp app is itself non-deletable, so a fixed pointer cannot rot.

methods.name: post_signed_price
methods.desc:
Publish a signed price. **Callable by anyone** — there is no sender check.
That is the point of the whole design. A liquidator submits [post_signed_price, trigger_*_liquidation] atomically, lp_ts_ is written in the same block the vault reads it, and the price is zero seconds old — so the vault's 1800s freshness window can never be the reason a liquidation fails.
Anyone posting costs them ~0.004 ALGO and overwrites existing keys. No unprivileged action creates state (add_pool is admin-only), so there is no MBR growth and no denial surface: a spammer pays to keep us fresh.
Checks run CHEAPEST FIRST. The bindings cost 49 opcode units together against 1900 for the signature (both measured), so a payload aimed somewhere else fails for 49 and reports why, instead of exhausting the budget and reporting that.

methods.name: add_pool
methods.desc:
Register a pool and seed a price, so the vault's `price > 0` assert is
never hit in the gap before the first relayed post.

methods.name: remove_pool
methods.desc:
Delist a pool and delete its state.
WARNING: removing a pool with active vaults borrowing against it makes their price stale and blocks health-factor liquidations (AUD-046).

methods.name: admin_set_price
methods.desc:
BREAK-GLASS. Write a price the signer did not produce. Every use should
be explained.
It exists because under this design staleness self-heals — anyone can post — so the failure that would otherwise force a retreat is a POSTING bug: a wrong pinned key, a wrong target_app, a payload nobody can make valid. Then nobody can post at all, and repointing the vault back takes 48 hours during which borrowing and liquidation are both dead. That is worse than any freeze this design removes.
It grants the admin nothing new: `remove_pool` followed by `add_pool` has always been an arbitrary admin price write, in two transactions. Naming it makes the capability auditable instead of leaving it an undocumented workaround that looks like routine pool maintenance.

methods.name: propose_signer
methods.desc:
Queue a signer-key rotation. Timelocked for the same reason the vault
timelocks its oracle repoint: an instantly-settable signer key would be a one-transaction takeover for a compromised admin.

methods.name: confirm_signer
methods.desc: Apply a queued rotation once the timelock has elapsed.

methods.name: cancel_pending_signer
methods.desc: Cancel a queued rotation. Admin or guardian — the guardian veto.

methods.name: propose_admin
methods.desc: Start 2-step admin rotation. Admin OR guardian (guardian = recovery).

methods.name: accept_admin
methods.desc: Complete admin rotation — only the proposed account may accept.

methods.name: accept_guardian
methods.desc: Complete guardian rotation — only the proposed account may accept.

methods.name: get_lp_price
methods.desc:
(price_scaled, issued_at) for pool_id, or (0, 0) if unregistered.
The vault does not use this — it reads lp_price_<pool_id> straight out of global state by cross-app reference, which is what makes this a drop-in replacement for the posted-price oracle.

desc:
Prices Tinyman LP tokens in mUSD (x 10^6), from signed payloads relayed by
    anyone. Drop-in for the posted-price oracle: same lp_price_ / lp_ts_ keys.
